comments.body:
100% agree CBC mode is legacy. 

No integrity without a MAC, vulnerable from padding oracle attacks, requires a unique *unpredictable* IV (unlike GCM), POODLE vulnerability...

It's super legacy.

NIST are calling for revising 800-38A. https://csrc.nist.gov/news/2022/proposal-to-revise-sp-800-38a

“ NIST plans to develop guidance about the incorporation of authentication into confidentiality applications, while considering exceptions for widely used protocols if countermeasures exist to mitigate vulnerabilities.”

So the way I read that is that, once the publication has been revised, there will be a clear recommendation on using authentication based cipher modes unless you have taken appropriate countermeasures. In other words, CBC will become deprecated.
